source_text: Macte virtute sapientiae, qui novae et a te inventae primum disputationis regulis, secunda primorum negatione complecteris, et corpora capitibus trunca componis. Non invidemus subtilitatibus tuis; quin immo christiana humanitate miseramur, quod dignum reperisti exitum dogmati tuo, ut profectus a criminibus innocentum, ad nihilum pervenires.
pass_a_gloss: Hail by the virtue of wisdom, you who by the rules of a new disputation first invented by you embrace seconds by the negation of firsts, and compose bodies truncated from heads. We do not envy your subtleties; nay rather by Christian humanity let us pity, that you found an end worthy of your dogma, that having set out from charges of innocents you arrived at nothing.
pass_b_english: Well done for your mighty wisdom! By the rules of a new method of argument first invented by you, you embrace conclusions by denying their premises, and assemble bodies severed from their heads. We do not envy your subtleties. Rather, with Christian kindness we pity you: you have found an ending worthy of your doctrine, departing from accusations against the innocent and arriving at nothing.

choices.english: sense taken from the locked Augustinus.it Latin
choices.why: Load-bearing wording in Julian's Latin; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
